Title: September 3, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Regular Meeting

Topic1.Title: Special Meeting: Executive Session on Open Space Legal Advice
Topic1.Summary: The council convened a special meeting and voted unanimously to enter executive session to receive confidential legal advice regarding authorized uses of city open space. The executive session was held under Colorado Revised Statutes and city charter provisions. Upon return to the public meeting, participants were listed and no concerns about improper discussion were raised. The special meeting then concluded.

Topic2.Title: Public Comment on Frasier Meadows Expansion, Panka Place Vacation, and Other Community Concerns
Topic2.Summary: Numerous residents spoke during open comment, with many opposing the Frasier Meadows expansion, requesting a public hearing on the project, and opposing the vacation of Panka Place. Speakers also raised concerns about BVSD school closures, party houses and student rentals, bear activity, Spruce Pool funding, and a proposed duplex development. Several speakers addressed Gaza and other issues, and an elementary student spoke against the closure of Flat Irons Elementary. Staff responded to questions and committed to follow-up on several issues.

Topic3.Title: Declarations Honoring Mark Wallik and Pollinator Appreciation Month
Topic3.Summary: Council read a declaration honoring former council member Mark Wallik for his seven years of service, and Mark responded with remarks. A second declaration recognized September 2026 as Pollinator Appreciation Month, featuring a demonstration of the Boulder bee biomonitoring initiative. The initiative uses honeybee hives and native bee homes to collect environmental data across the community.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda and Employee Evaluations
Topic4.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda 8 to 0, with one member voting nay on item 4E. Item 4E covered the 2025-26 performance evaluations and salary adjustments for the city manager, city attorney, and municipal court judge. Council members praised the employees' performance and expressed concerns about the evaluation process and oversight.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins for Frasier Meadows and Excel Energy Facility
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed a site review amendment for Frasier Meadows at 350 and 355 Panka Place, which proposes a 55-foot senior housing building, and a councilmember moved to call it up, but no second was made. Council also reviewed a concept plan for expanding the Xcel Energy facility at 2655 North 63rd Street, and no call-up was requested. Staff responded to questions about public access, flood mitigation, inclusionary housing fees, and energy use.

Topic6.Title: Public Hearing: Ordinance 8757 on Pedal Cab Licensing
Topic6.Summary: Council held a public hearing and second reading on Ordinance 8757, which establishes agency and driver licenses for pedal cabs. Staff explained that the framework covers qualifications, insurance, and operating rules, with enforcement authority for the city manager. Council discussed fee revenue, enforcement on CU campus, and wage requirements before approving the ordinance 7 to 0.

Topic7.Title: Matters from the City Manager: State Legislation on Housing
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented three state housing laws for informational discussion: Proposition 123 affordable housing funding, the transit-oriented communities bill, and the Home Act. Staff explained that these laws require faster review timelines and may lead to code changes such as removing planning board call-ups for qualifying projects. Council gave non-binding direction to pursue several proposed changes, including removing call-ups for form-based code reviews and affordable housing projects with at least 50 percent affordable units.

Topic8.Title: Matters from Mayor and Council: Restaurant Task Force and County Ballot Measure
Topic8.Summary: Council members Matt Benjamin and Tara Winer proposed a small restaurant and worker dialogue group to build relationships and explore solutions, and council unanimously supported moving forward. Council also discussed a Boulder County ballot measure to expand the board of county commissioners from three to five members. After discussion, council voted five to three to take a support position on the measure.
